No — they don't collide, because the title isn't the whole slug. `ArticleService.slugify()` appends a random suffix:

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts:201-203
slugify(title: string) {
  return slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + (Math.random() * Math.pow(36, 6) | 0).toString(36)
}
```

So two "How I Learned Rust" articles become `how-i-learned-rust-1kf3zq` and `how-i-learned-rust-9x2ab0`. Uniqueness comes from ~2.18 billion random values, not from the title.

That said, three things are worth knowing:

**Nothing actually enforces uniqueness.** `slug` is a plain `@Column()` with no unique index (`src/article/article.entity.ts:11-12`). A random draw over 36⁶ makes accidental collisions unlikely — roughly 0.02% at 1,000 same-titled articles, ~2% at 10,000 — but if one happens the DB accepts it silently. Then `findOne({slug})` (`article.service.ts:166`, `:191`) returns whichever row the DB hands back first, and `delete()` at `:198` does `DELETE FROM article WHERE slug = ?`, which removes **every** matching row, not just one.

**The likelier collision isn't random, it's deliberate.** `update()` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, articleData)` (`:192`) with no field whitelist, and the controller's `@Put(':slug')` has no `ValidationPipe` (`article.controller.ts:59-63`). A client can `PUT` an `article.slug` field and set their slug to any string — including one that already belongs to someone else. Same for `id`, `author`, and `favoriteCount`.

Related: that's also why the `// Todo: update slug also when title gets changed` on line 61 lingers — renaming an article leaves the old title in the URL.

**Minor bug in the suffix itself.** `36^6 = 2,176,782,336` exceeds the 32-bit signed max (`2,147,483,647`), and `| 0` coerces to int32. About 1.3% of the time the value wraps negative, so the slug gets a double dash: `how-i-learned-rust--4kz9`. Ugly rather than dangerous, but it's unintended.

Worth flagging separately: neither `update` nor `delete` checks that the caller owns the article — the controller never reads the user id on those routes. Any authenticated user can edit or delete any article by slug, collision or not. That's a bigger problem than the slug question.

Want me to fix any of these — a unique index plus retry-on-collision, the mass-assignment hole, or the ownership check?
